extraAngles.prompt: THE PROCEDURAL-GENERATION BASELINE (owner GO 2026-09-07 ~02:20; the one angle the ai critic says changes the reconstruction rules): SettlementForge's dossier is a procedurally generated record built from typed pools, and the literature on that architecture measured this exact failure — perceptual sameness under mathematical variety — long before language models. ZERO rows exist. Roster, each fetched RAW and quoted (≤ 12 words per quote): Kate Compton, 'So you want to build a generator…' (galaxykate0.tumblr.com, 22 Feb 2016; the 10,000 bowls of oatmeal; perceptual differentiation vs. mathematical uniqueness; the 'possibility space'; constraints as generative); Jason Grinblat & Brian Bucklew, 'Subverting historical cause & effect: generation of mythic biographies in Caves of Qud' (FDG 2017; pcgworkshop.com/archive/grinblat2017subverting.pdf; ACM 10.1145/3102071.3110574) and Grinblat's 'Generating Histories' chapter in Procedural Generation in Game Design (CRC 2019; search-inside or the authors' talks/slides); Tarn Adams on Dwarf Fortress Legends mode and history generation (Gamasutra/Game Developer interviews, the DF Talk transcripts, Roguelike Celebration talks); James Ryan, 'Talk of the Town' / 'Bad News' and the 2018 UCSC dissertation 'Curating Simulated Storyworlds' (escholarship.org); Mark R. Johnson, Ultima Ratio Regum's dev blog on generated cultures, religions and books; Gillian Smith & Jim Whitehead, 'Analyzing the Expressive Range of a Level Generator' (PCG workshop 2010; expressive-range histograms as the measurement of sameness); plus Emily Short's 'Bowls of Oatmeal and Text Generation' (emshort.blog, Feb 2016) and Max Kreminski's work on 'why are we like this' / generative story sifting if reachable. For EACH source: what it says sameness IS (the mechanism), how it MEASURED it (the instrument), and what cured or worsened it (constraints, history, fixed points, canon, sifting). Mark the register each finding was measured in (game text, generated history, level design). Lawful routes only (author sites, arXiv/eScholarship/ACM abstracts, conference archives, Wayback); routeHint on every claim. Cap 70 claims; complete:true when the roster is exhausted.
